brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;half-n and piece:0,0,1;half-n stacked, with a top cover (about 160 mm tall).

A small standalone stack whose two drawers can hold small tools and parts; shown with M3 screws in the open drawer and gaffer tape on the top. Faces are capped. Adding joint bolts changed nothing, so there are none.
drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:1#0,0#cut, one in each storey.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey storage tower with two drawers. It's two north-half hex bases stacked at cell (0,0), levels 0 and 1, with a drawer in the open cut face of each. A top cover closes the upper storey, and 5 solid end caps close the other open faces. Adding joint bolts changed nothing ("lockJoints" made no change), so the build has none. That comes to 23 parts, about 1229 g of filament and 1770 minutes of printing. The final check found no rule errors, and the mesh-collision check came back clear. For display, the bottom drawer is shown open with a small pile of M3 screws in it. The pile sits below the drawer rim, so it's only partly visible. A roll of gaffer tape is on the top cover. I couldn't stand up a hex driver, pencil or marker in the open drawer: the configurator said they wouldn't stay put. The two drawers have no handles; I didn't check whether handles would fit on them.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
